Another notable meteor event occurred on November 17, 1833 CE, but unlike the 1479 CE event, the 1833 CE meteors were sporadic. ______ the meteors appeared randomly from various points in the sky, rather than radiating from a single constellation.
questions.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.text: For example,
That is,
Meanwhile,
Nonetheless,

explanation.summary: The second sentence restates what "sporadic" means for the 1833 meteors: they appeared randomly rather than radiating from one constellation. That is a definition of the word just used.

choices.A: "For example" introduces an instance, but this sentence explains the term instead of illustrating it with a case.
choices.B: Correct. "That is" introduces the restatement that defines "sporadic."
choices.C: "Meanwhile" marks something happening at the same time elsewhere, not a clarification.
choices.D: "Nonetheless" concedes a contrast, and the sentence agrees with what precedes it.

passage: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Big Cypress National Preserve is a protected natural area in Florida.
• It encompasses 729,000 acres.
• It was established to safeguard the habitat of the Florida panther, an endangered species.
• The Big Cypress National Preserve is managed by the National Park Service.
• The National Park Service restricts off-road vehicle use in the area.
questions.stem: The student wants to indicate the size of the Big Cypress National Preserve. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: A protected natural area, the Big Cypress National Preserve encompasses 729,000 acres of land in Florida.
The Big Cypress National Preserve is a natural area in Florida, home to the Florida panther.
Home to the Florida panther, Florida's Big Cypress National Preserve is managed by the National Park Service.
The Big Cypress National Preserve is a protected natural area managed by the National Park Service, which restricts off-road vehicle use there.

explanation.summary: The goal is to indicate the size of the preserve, so the choice has to carry the acreage from the notes.

choices.A: Correct. It gives the 729,000-acre figure, which is the size the student wants to convey.
choices.B: It names the location and the panther but never the size.
choices.C: It covers management and the panther, with no acreage.
choices.D: It focuses on management and vehicle restrictions instead of size.

passage: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Urban Margins is a 2016 photographic work by Canadian artist Ethan Walsh.
• It is created from black-and-white images that capture documentary street scenes.
• Constructed Dreams No. 3 is a 2021 photographic work by Japanese artist Yuki Tanaka.
• It is created from color images that depict staged conceptual scenes.
questions.stem: The student wants to emphasize a difference between the two photographic works. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.text: Ethan Walsh and Yuki Tanaka are artists who have used photography in their work.
Both Walsh's and Tanaka's photographic works are created from images.
Unlike Walsh's work, which captures documentary scenes, Tanaka's depicts staged conceptual scenes.
Urban Margins, like Constructed Dreams No. 3, is a photographic work.

explanation.summary: The goal is a difference. The notes contrast black-and-white documentary street scenes with color staged conceptual scenes, so the choice has to set the two works against each other.

choices.A: Both artists using photography is a similarity, not a difference.
choices.B: Both works being made from images is also a similarity.
choices.C: Correct. "Unlike Walsh’s work" sets documentary scenes against Tanaka’s staged conceptual ones.
choices.D: "Like Constructed Dreams No. 3" states what the works share.

passage: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• The Olympic Games are a series of international sporting events involving athletes from around the world.
• A gold medal indicates that an athlete finished in first place.
• Yuki Tanaka competed as an Olympic sprinter from 1992 to 2004.
• He won eleven medals, eight of which were gold.
• Elena Volkov competed as an Olympic long jumper from 1996 to 2008.
• She won nineteen medals, sixteen of which were gold.
questions.stem: Which choice most effectively uses information from the given sentences to emphasize how long Elena Volkov competed in the Olympic Games?

choices.text: During her career as an Olympic long jumper, Elena Volkov took home a total of nineteen medals, sixteen of which were gold.
An accomplished Olympian with multiple gold medal wins, Elena Volkov competed as a long jumper from 1996 to 2008.
Long jump, a sport in which Elena Volkov took home sixteen gold medals, has been an event at the Olympic Games since 1896.
Sprinter Yuki Tanaka made his Olympic debut in 1992, while long jumper Elena Volkov made her debut in 1996.

explanation.summary: The goal is how long Volkov competed, so the choice has to give the span of her career: 1996 to 2008.

choices.A: It emphasizes her medal count and gives no dates.
choices.B: Correct. It states that she competed as a long jumper from 1996 to 2008, which is the length of her career.
choices.C: The 1896 claim is not in the notes, and the sentence is about the sport rather than her career span.
choices.D: It gives both athletes’ debut years but never says when Volkov stopped competing.
